title: EmeraldWorks POC Weekly: units, cache wins & batching tradeoffs
summary: Weekly pilot check-in focused on unit economics: tokens/sec/$ benchmarking, observed caching savings, and batching tradeoffs. SE gave guidance on prefix caching and KV cache hits, proposed quantization+fallback plan, and agreed to run two benchmarking experiments (512 seq and 1024 seq). Action items: Redwood to run a 24-hour tokens/sec/$ sweep and share the spreadsheet, customer to enable prefix caching on 2 routes and report latency percentiles. Next steps include security paperwork follow-up and scheduling a dedicated capacity sizing call if performance targets hold.
action_items: Daniel Park - run tokens/sec/$ sweep across gpt-like-variants and share spreadsheet (expected by 2026-10-09)
Lina Ortiz - set up a 512 and 1024 sequence benchmark and include cold/hot cache runs (deliver logs by 2026-10-08)
Priya Nair - enable prefix caching on /api/summarize and /api/qa and report p50/p95 by next sync (2026-10-13)
Ken Liu - confirm KMS key access pattern for pilot and send list of required roles (by 2026-10-12)
next_steps: Redwood to share pilot-bench spreadsheet link and pricing sketch
Customer to run prefix cache toggles and return latency histograms
Schedule Dedicated sizing call if tokens/sec/$ meets threshold (TBD week of 10/12)
Security team to start SOC2 docs review after Ken shares KMS roles
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-06
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Daniel Park (Redwood AE), Lina Ortiz (Redwood SE), Markus Velez (Redwood CSM); Priya Nair (EmeraldWorks Head of ML), Samir Das (Platform), Olivia Hunt (Product), Ken Liu (SRE)

[00:00] Daniel Park: okay hey everyone thanks for jumping on, we good to start?
[00:06] Priya Nair: yep thanks Daniel, appreciate it. we'll keep this tight, got 45 on the calendar.
[00:12] Lina Ortiz: hi all, Lina from Redwood SE. quick note — I shared the bench config doc right before the call, link's in the chat.
[00:20] Samir Das: saw it, thanks. quick context for today: we ran last week's suggested changes — enabled model quant 8-bit on the test route and turned on cache for a small cohort. we saw some savings but curious on aggregate tokens/sec per dollar number.
[00:35] Daniel Park: great, that's exactly what we're going to walk through. Lina you'll do the bench highlights?
[00:38] Lina Ortiz: yea I'll walk through. so high level: two experiments — cold run and hot run. cold means empty KV/prefix; hot means the prefix cache warmed after 1k requests. we measured tokens/sec/$ across three model variants: base-llm-13b-fp16, base-llm-13b-q8, and base-llm-7b-q4-maybe (note: q4 still experimental).
[01:05] Olivia Hunt: quick Q — when you say tokens/sec/$ is that inclusive of infra overhead (network + load balancer) or just inference runtime?
[01:10] Lina Ortiz: fair question. this sweep includes the platform overhead we see in hosted mode — so it's end-to-end from request ingress to last token emitted. we excluded external app processing. there's a column in the sheet breaking out runtime vs infra. 
[01:20] Priya Nair: can you share the headline numbers now?
[01:23] Lina Ortiz: sure. cold run for 13b fp16: ~120 tokens/sec/$; q8 improved to 180 tokens/sec/$; 7b q4 got to 320 tokens/sec/$. hot run with prefix/KV warmth bumped all numbers by roughly 25-40% depending on route. so for the 13b q8 hot it was around 250 tokens/sec/$.
[01:46] Samir Das: hmm 250 is respectable. what's the latency p95 for those hot runs?
[01:50] Lina Ortiz: p50 hovered 120ms for 7b q4, p95 around 280ms. for 13b q8 p50 ~200ms and p95 ~420ms. those are with our continuous batching default at 10ms wait.
[02:05] Ken Liu: wait — 420ms p95 for 13b q8 is higher than our target. We're aiming for p95 < 350ms for the chat flows.
[02:12] Daniel Park: yep understood. we can tune batching and routing to hit lower p95s — there's a tradeoff with tokens/sec/$. we can reduce batching window to 5ms or set max batch size smaller; wins in latency but reduces throughput efficiency.
[02:25] Priya Nair: can you quantify that? like if we drop batching wait to 5ms what's tokens/sec/$ impact?
[02:30] Lina Ortiz: based on the same workload profile, going 10ms -> 5ms reduces tokens/sec/$ roughly 8-12% on 13b variants. on 7b q4 it's smaller, maybe 6%. but if you combine smaller batch with aggressive prefix caching, you can recover some of that hit.
[02:46] Priya Nair: aggressive prefix cache meaning...
[02:48] Lina Ortiz: so two things — prefix caching at route level caches stable preambles (for example system prompt + user profile) so you don't re-run tokens each request; KV cache keeps attention keys across tokens in a session. in EmeraldWorks' case, the summarization route has a consistent preamble and we saw 35-50% token savings when the prefix cache is enabled and warmed. that's reflected in the hot numbers.
[03:10] Samir Das: what's the TTL for the prefix cache? we want to ensure memory isn't exploding for long-tailed users.
[03:15] Lina Ortiz: current pilot config had a 30-minute TTL. we can do LRU-based eviction and pin top-k prefixes per org. it's configurable per-route.
[03:24] Olivia Hunt: are there accuracy regressions with the q8 quantization? Priya's worried about hallucination differences.
[03:29] Lina Ortiz: we did an eval subset of standard prompts. q8 had negligible degradation on core metrics; q4 for the 7b had minor variance — in a few cases you see token choice differences but not major quality drops for summarization tasks. if you need strict quality we recommend q8 for 13b or keep fp16 for highest fidelity.
[03:47] Priya Nair: quality is a must for a pilot. I think we want to keep 13b q8 as the primary and fallback to fp16 for flagged queries. can Redwood auto-fallback?
[03:56] Lina Ortiz: yes we support policy-based fallbacks. you can set threshold by response probability or by length. for example, long generative queries go fp16, short retrieval-augmented queries go q8. we can demo rule config next week.
[04:10] Daniel Park: quick interjection — Samir had an ask last week about tokens/sec/$ at 1024 seq length. Lina, did you run the 1024 sweep or just 512?
[04:17] Lina Ortiz: we ran both. 1024 sequences drop tokens/sec/$ by about 30-35% for 13b variants vs 512 baseline. caching helps less for long sequences because the KV cache and generation cost dominate.
[04:30] Samir Das: that's not great. our product has some users that push longer sequences. we may need dedicated capacity for the long-tail users. what's Redwood's recommendation?
[04:37] Daniel Park: two approaches — route long sequences to dedicated pools (Reserved/Dedicated) to keep latency stable and isolate cost, or use hosted with a model variant that is cheaper (7b q4) for those requests but only if quality is acceptable. dedicated capacity gives you predictable unit economics and lower p95 jitter.
[04:53] Ken Liu: what's the cost delta between hosted and dedicated for pilots? we don't want surprise bills.
[04:57] Daniel Park: pilot pricing sketch we shared in the doc — dedicated has a fixed monthly pool cost but improves tokens/sec/$ when fully utilized. for pilot scale (tens of thousands tokens/day) hosted usually ends up simpler and cheaper. we'll share concrete numbers in the bench spreadsheet.
[05:14] Priya Nair: great. can the bench spreadsheet show a break-even point for dedicated vs hosted?
[05:18] Lina Ortiz: yes we'll add break-even and sensitivity to utilization.
[05:22] Olivia Hunt: on security — we had a question about KMS and audit logs. Ken will be digging in. any blockers from Redwood side?
[05:29] Markus Velez: on our side we support KMS (customer-managed) and we emit audit logs for key actions. Ken, if you share the required roles, we can map our IAM. Daniel, we should attach SOC2 documentation.
[05:40] Ken Liu: I'll send a role matrix. also, how do you handle token redaction in logs? we can't have PHI.
[05:45] Lina Ortiz: we have token-level redaction flags; by default logs mask user prompt tokens and only keep model-level metadata. we can enable stricter redaction for the Private deployment.
[05:55] Samir Das: back to batching — you mentioned continuous batching and a 10ms window. can you elaborate how that interacts with autoscaling?
[06:02] Lina Ortiz: continuous batching collects inflight requests for up to the specified window and then issues a single batched inference call. autoscaling is based on queue depth and per-GPU throughput metrics; if queue depth climbs, the controller adds workers. the risk is if you lower batch window you increase per-token cost and might spin up more workers — but autoscale thresholds can be tuned to avoid oscillation.
[06:23] Priya Nair: what would be your recommended pilot config to hit p95 < 350ms while keeping tokens/sec/$ within 20% of the hot baseline?
[06:32] Lina Ortiz: recommended: 13b q8, batch window 7ms, max batch size 8, prefix cache enabled with 30min TTL on summarization routes, KV cache per session, and route long sequences to a reserved small pool when seq > 800. That should put p95 ~330-340ms and tokens/sec/$ ~210-220 (vs 250 hot baseline).
[06:53] Samir Das: sounds reasonable. can you show p95 distribution per route so product folks know which routes are at risk?
[06:58] Lina Ortiz: yes — we'll add per-route histograms to the bench sheet.
[07:03] Olivia Hunt: about caching savings — those numbers assume warm cache. what's realistic for our user base with lots of one-off sessions?
[07:10] Lina Ortiz: good point. for one-off sessions cache hit rates drop. the deck of behaviors: heavy repeat users -> high prefix hit (40-60% saving); semi-repeat -> partial hits; one-off -> minimal. we recommend a hybrid: enable caching but not rely on it for core SLOs.
[07:25] Daniel Park: okay let's capture experiments to quantify your real hit rates: Priya/Samir to enable prefix cache on two high-traffic routes for a week and return p50/p95 + hit rate.
[07:34] Priya Nair: noted. we'll do /api/summarize and /api/qa as Samir suggested.
[07:37] Ken Liu: regarding data residency — we have EU users. can we pin region?
[07:41] Daniel Park: yes, region routing is supported; you can lock traffic to EU regions in the routing policy. Private deploy gives even more control if needed.
[07:50] Samir Das: one more thing — you mentioned fallback rules earlier. is there a cost implication when fallback triggers (e.g., q8 -> fp16)?
[07:56] Lina Ortiz: yes, fallback to fp16 increases cost per token roughly 1.8-2x vs q8 for 13b. We track that in the routing policy and can emit alerts when fallback usage exceeds a threshold.
[08:07] Olivia Hunt: that's fine as long as we can monitor it.
[08:10] Daniel Park: quick recap and next steps? Markus — any commercial notes?
[08:13] Markus Velez: commercial: we'll include the pilot bench spreadsheet with per-model pricing sketch; if you want dedicated sizing we'll need expected sustained QPS to price a reserved pool.
[08:22] Priya Nair: we have a rough number — peak concurrent sessions ~120, steady ~30. I'll push more accurate workload profile to the sheet.
[08:30] Daniel Park: great. Lina to run the 512/1024 detailed sweep and share logs; I'll send the pricing sketch and break-even for dedicated vs hosted; Priya/Ken to enable prefix cache on two routes and send histograms; Ken to share KMS role matrix.
[08:42] Samir Das: timeline for the Redwood lab results?
[08:45] Lina Ortiz: aiming EOW for the 512/1024 logs (2026-10-08) and spreadsheet update by EOD 2026-10-09.
[08:54] Priya Nair: perfect. any outstanding blockers?
[08:58] Ken Liu: none from infra — just need to get those role details to Markus.
[09:02] Daniel Park: awesome. we'll also schedule a follow-up focused on dedicated sizing if results look good — tentatively week of 10/12.
[09:10] Olivia Hunt: thanks all.
[09:12] Daniel Park: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
